- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days), then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 82.31 → 85+), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates when true values are near or below 80–82, particularly after a recent high.
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts drift toward historical mean too early, missing sustained trends.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true drop.
- Overreacts to minor historical fluctuations (e.g., 78.54 → 82.31) by forecasting large jumps.
- Underestimates when true values are clustered near 78–82, especially if history includes recent low values.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the final 5–10 days, often missing sharp downward corrections.
- Model fails to capture “recovery” patterns after sharp declines — assumes continuation rather than reversal.
- Overestimates volatility in the middle of the forecast, then underestimates in the tail.
